title.narrative: Ensuring Inclusiveness and Service Delivery for Persons with Disabilities Project

description.narrative: Often, public support to persons with disabilities (PWDs) focus on providing assistance under the concept of social welfare. However, this project will highlight what PWDs can do to ensure inclusion of PWDs in society, including them in mainstream economic activities, creating opportunities in education and employment, and providing access to the services they need. It will strengthen and institutionalize early identification of disability; improve service delivery and access to the physical environment; improve employment prospects; and contribute to strategic development for PWDs, including social welfare reform, awareness raising, and attitude change.

title.narrative: 29 Nov 2017 | News Release: https://www.adb.org/news/adb-loan-help-improve-inclusiveness-quality-life-people-disabilities-mongolia
Grant 9191: 93% of contracts awarded and 91% disbursed as of 28 Apr 2025
Loan 3605: 68% of contracts awarded and 69% disbursed as of 28 Apr 2025

Progress Toward Outcome: The project aims to increase access to services and employment for PWDs. The project will (i) institutionalize new models for early identification of delays in children's development, (ii) improve service delivery for PWD in rural areas by establishing the Development Centers in 6 aimags, (iii) improve access to physical environment through changes in regulations and policies, (iv) improve employment opportunities for PWD by establishing the Employment Resource Center in Ulaanbaatar, and (v) support PWDs and social welfare reforms through communication campaign. The project experienced implementation delays in 2018-2019 due to slow start-up and recruitment of the PIU staff. The COVID-19 pandemic has significantly impacted the implementation of the project in 2020-2021, especially the provision of technical outputs by international and national consultants. Currently, the implementation of the project is progressing well.
Some results are in the Audited Project Financial Statements | Jul 2024: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/48076/48076-002-apfs-en_4.pdf
Some results are in the Initial Environmental Examination | Aug 2024: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/48076/48076-002-iee-en_0.pdf
Some results are in the Safeguards Due Diligence Reports | Jan 2025: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/48076/48076-002-sddr-en_0.pdf

Status of Implementation Progress: Output 1. Early identification of children with disabilities strengthened and institutionalized.
The project aims to (a) institutionalize the new models of early identification of delays in children's development and (b) facilitate the shift by broadening the skills of relevant professionals involved in the early identification system. Consultant C2 (MCDS Consultancy LLC) assessed the current situation with the early identification system and developed a Mongolian version of ASQ or Mongolian Rapid Baby Assessment Scale (MORBAS) for children aged 9, 18, and 36 months, pre-tested it in six project sites and Ulaanbaatar and incorporated the questionnaire into the Child Health Handbook or 'Pink Book, which was approved by MOH in June 2023. MLSP and MOH agreed to use Dr. Baumann's tool for a secondary-level confirmatory assessment of developmental delays and signed a contract with Dr. Bauman in April 2023 for contextualizing the tool into Mongolian, training and capacity building, and technical assistance. Implementation is ongoing. Consultants assisted in improving functions of the multisectoral commissions responsible for the disability assessment of children. In 2021, the MLSP, MES, and MOH jointly approved a decree to endorse revised guidelines and methodology for the development assessment and assistance for CWD to be used by multisectoral commissions. In 2022, the project trained members of the multisectoral commission in project aimags and Ulaanbaatar on newly approved guidelines and methodology.
Output 2. Service delivery for persons with disabilities improved.
The project aims to (a) establish the Development Centers (DCs) for PWD in six aimags with a broad range of services, including physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, optometry, basic orthopedic services, portage service - an interactive parent-child-facilitator home-based teaching program for CWD, and other social services; and (b) introduce and/or update the existing curricula in physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, optometry and orthopedy and assist in establishing a disability workforce.
In April 2020, MLSP recruited a consulting firm, C1 (JV MSL LLC and Creative Mongolia LLC), who prepared the Detailed Engineering Design (DED) of DCs following the universal design requirements. Construction of DCs in six project aimags commenced in JuneJuly 2021. As of September 2023, five DCs have been constructed (in Darkhan-uul, Dundgovi, Dornod, Khovd, and Khuvsgul aimags). Construction of DC in Arkhangai aimag is significantly delayed, with a progress of 50%. In June 2023, MLSP terminated the contract with the contractor (JV of Jam LLC and Motoblok LLC). MLSP is preparing to re-bid the remaining work at Arkhangai aimag DC.
Procurement of equipment for six DCs, including furniture, assistive technology, IT, and orthopedic equipment, has been completed. Furniture (42 types, 1026 pieces, $172,497) and equipment (131 types, 1470 pieces, $1.72 million) were delivered and installed in March 2023.
Consultant C2 developed the service delivery design and operational guidelines for the DCs. In June 2021, the government issued Decree No.164 on establishing DCs in six project aimags as a government-owned public entity under the GADPWD as an oversight body. In July 2022, the MLSP issued order A/159 to approve the rules and structure of DCs for PWD. The DCs will have 29 staff, including 13 administrative and 16 technical staff.
Consultant C2 analyzed the qualifications required for disability workforce and their training opportunities, reviewed the existing training curricula at various training institutions, and developed (i) communication teacher's curricula (or speech therapy) and (ii) disability social workers' curricula for the Mongolian State University of Education, (iii) peer counseling curricula for the Universal Development NGO, (iv) assistive technology technician's curricula for the National Prosthetic Factory, and (v) low vision specialist curricula for the Mongolian Ophthalmologist Association. Consultant C2 also updated (vi) physical therapy and occupational therapy curricula for the School of Nursing of the Mongolian National University of Medical Sciences. The project trained potential candidates for a new team of six DCs through seven training with the participation of 348 people (132 from six project aimags). The selection and recruitment of the team for DCs are ongoing; the project will continue training the DC staff.
In 2021, the MLSP established the Social Protection Call Center to communicate and provide information for PWD. As of April 2023, 20818 calls were received and responded to.
Output 3. Access to the physical environment improved.
The project will (a) develop the capacity of decision-makers and strengthen institutions involved in developing and enforcing the legal and regulatory framework on physical accessibility norms (infrastructure, transportation, and information), (b) ensure participation of PWD in enforcement mechanisms, and (c) ensure access to affordable quality orthopedic devices and assistive technology. In March 2020, MLSP engaged the consulting firm C3 (HRD Consulting Korea Co., Ltd), which developed recommendations to improve legislation, regulations, and accessibility-related standards for construction, road and transportation, information communication, health, and social services. This includes recommendations and proposals for the revision of (i) the Law on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (2016), and (ii) the National Program on the Rights, Inclusiveness and Support for PWD. Consultant C3 also assisted MLSP in drafting a new bill on improving the accessibility for the disabled. Consultant C3 also conducted reality checks with the support of DPOs to identify accessibility barriers and prepared a report with findings from a comparison of 2015 and 2020 accessibility audits.
Consultants C6 reviewed the regulatory framework for assistive technologies and devices (AT) and prostheses in Mongolia, the roles and capacity of the prosthesis factory and vocational training center for PWD, and developed a mid-term development strategy for AT. The project is upgrading the capacity of the Orthopedic and Prosthesis Factory and the Vocational Training Center for PWD. The project built a new ventilation system and procured equipment (61 types, 201 pieces, $425,510) and spare parts for existing Ottobock machines. The project consultant assisted in developing a development strategy for the Vocational Training Center for PWD and procured and installed AT-related equipment and training tools for the Vocational Training Center in June 2023. The project consultant also assisted in developing a training program and materials for a sign language interpreter course at the Vocational Training Center for PWD. In 2020, the project renovated the training room at the MLSP to make it accessible for PWD.
To ensure access to information for PWD, the project developed the Mongolian text-to-speech software to make government and public websites accessible for PWD, especially those with hearing and visual imparities. The development of the text-to-speech system was completed in March 2023.
Output 4. Work and employment for PWD improved.
The project aims to (a) set up models to increase PWDs' skills to enter selected industries and improve general job matching and brokerage, (b) organize support systems for PWDs to access regular jobs and improve self-employment. The project is establishing the Employment Resource Center (ERC) for PWD in Ulaanbaatar. The concept design and DED were prepared and approved in 2021. The construction of ERC started in April 2022; as of September 2023, the work progress is estimated at 60%.
Consultant C3 reviewed the current situation and developed (i) a model of partnership and cooperation between the employment services run by DPOs and public employment services with the focus of providing job coaching and job brokering services for PWDs, (ii) job profiles and job descriptions for staff in charge of delivering employment services for PWD, (iii) guidelines for job coaching, and brokering services, and (iv) recommendations to improve the system of monitoring and evaluation, and reporting on the implementation of employment promotion programs for PWD. Consultant C3 reviewed the implementation of the Labor Law (2021) and the Law on Employment Promotion (2011) concerning employment promotion for PWD and the quota system and proposed necessary changes regarding implementing the quota system.
Consultant C4 reviewed the international experience on the institutional models for an umbrella organization of DPOs and assisted in developing a business plan and development strategy, including organizational and management structure and human resources for the ERC to support PWD accessing employment services. The MLSP, with the technical and financial support of JICA, is implementing a technical assistance project on strengthening employment promotion services for PWDs. The JICA project will train staff at ERC through training planned in 2024.
Output 5. Strategic development to support PWD implemented.
The project will (a) raise awareness and change attitudes toward PWD, (b) improve targeting of social welfare assistance and financial support to access services and assistive technologies, (c) introduce the International Classification of Functioning (ICF) in line with available resources, and (d) align statistical data on disability with new classification and information needs. The project developed the Communication Strategy for awareness-raising and attitude change toward PWD to promote awareness-raising communication on the rights of PWD, social protection, employment opportunities, early identification, community-based rehabilitation services, reproductive rights of PWD, and inclusive employment for PWD. In 2021, MLSP contracted 7 national firms and DPOs to develop the content of awareness-raising programs with the participation of PWD. In 2021-2022, the communication campaign was organized through (i) public events and national campaigns, (ii) TV and radio programs, and (iii) mass media advertisements.
Consultant C3 conducted a SWAT analysis of multi-sectoral commissions concerning their readiness and capacity to use the International Classification of Functioning, Disability, and Health (ICF). Consultants reviewed the existing regulations, institutional arrangements, and human resources and proposed a simplified ICF model for assessing PWD's workability. In April 2023, MLSP and MOH established the ICF joint task force to finalize the ICF tools and methodological guidelines, pilot the simplified ICF tools for adults in project aimags, and develop recommendations on national roll-out.
In March 2020, MLSP hired two consultants (Consultant C7) to help them to review existing national population-based surveys, improve disability statistics, and assist the National Statistical Office (NSO) in developing appropriate tools to analyze data on the livelihood and living conditions of PWD. Consultant C7 reviewed the existing information, statistical data on disability in line with Washington Group recommendations, and the Household Socio-Economic Survey (HSES) considering the Incheon strategy on livelihoods and poverty of PWD, cash benefits, and coverage of social services, and, in 2021, developed recommendations on how to improve the disability statistics. In May 2022, MLSP and NSO established a joint working group to create an integrated database of disability statistics tools and forms based on the consultant's recommendation. The working group's follow-up actions are pending.
Tenders and Contracts Awarded: https://www.adb.org/projects/48076-002/main#project-tenders
